editorial.headline: Wholesale Vegetable Oils: Open Nationally, PMA-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale trade in vegetable oils, fats, margarine and vegetable-fat-based products is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
This activity is wholesale trading in vegetable oils and vegetable fats. The stated scope expressly includes margarine and products made from vegetable fats, with non-dairy creamer named as an example. It should therefore be read as a wholesale category that takes in the oils and fats themselves as well as the specifically named vegetable-fat-based products. The wording does not treat margarine or non-dairy creamer as outside additions: both sit within the activity’s stated scope. The commercial subject is the trade in that defined range of goods.

The registration picture starts broad by business scale. The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar, so stated availability is not confined to one of those four scales. Each is expressly included. This scale position sits alongside a nationally open PMA position. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In clear terms, the national ceiling permits complete foreign ownership. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is the source recorded for that national position. National openness is thus stated both in status and in the ownership ceiling.

Bali changes the result decisively for PMA registration. For a foreigner, registering this activity as PMA is not possible in Bali today. Its Bali status, Blocked (risk class), rests on a specific recorded reason: at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah on every scope. In English, those risk bands are Low and Medium-Low. That classification brings the activity within the Bali moratorium. This is not a generic Bali caveat: the record ties the PMA block directly to the risk reading across every scope at the Besar scale.

The moratorium began on May 13, 2026. It is island-wide and permanent, blocking PMA for all activities classified Low or Medium-Low risk; the record cites Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. That is why national and Bali positions cannot be collapsed into one answer. The national 100% figure remains a foreign-ownership ceiling; it does not displace Bali’s local PMA moratorium. For this wholesale activity, the exact conclusion is straightforward: nationally, it is open to foreign ownership up to 100%; in Bali, PMA registration is blocked under the permanent risk-based rule.
editorial.pullQuote: A 100% national ownership ceiling does not displace Bali’s permanent block on PMA registration.
